clue.text: Race can be a big subject

definitions.meaning: a horse race, the famous steeplechase run each year at Aintree
read literally, an important citizen of a country: a grand (big) national (subject)

explanation.surface: A horse race can make a large topic of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase, run at Aintree near Liverpool; 'subject' here means a citizen, not a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The words name the world-famous British steeplechase, and read literally describe an important citizen of a nation.

clue.text: There' not much to say when having it

definitions.text: There' not much to say when having it

parts.words: There' not much to say when having it
parts.note: someone possessing this quality keeps quiet and offers few words

explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in speech means saying little, which is exactly the quality the clue describes.

clue.text: Name formerly used for the present time

parts.note: once means at some time in the past

explanation.surface: A title that was once used for the current era.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the phrase 'for the nonce', meaning for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives in the idiom 'for the nonce', meaning just for the present occasion.

clue.text: Cuts on chest need treatment

indicators.note: letters needing treatment are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wounds on someone's torso require medical attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Small V-shaped cuts or nicks in a surface are a synonym for the plural noun.

clue.text: For wrapping or handkerchiefs — its uses are varied

indicators.note: uses that are varied are changed about, so those letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft paper product has many uses, from wrapping gifts to blowing noses.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin paper sheets used for wrapping gifts, and disposable paper handkerchiefs, both go by this word.

clue.text: Using the phone when one is at risk

definitions.meaning: in danger of being lost, as when a job is said to be in jeopardy

explanation.surface: Someone takes a call just when they are in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means connected on a telephone call, and idiomatically also means in jeopardy.

clue.text: Where Davy Crockett made his last stand, doctor-fashion

definitions.text: Where Davy Crockett made his last stand

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the fashion of
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Asking where a frontier hero died, phrased in a medical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor-fashion' reads as 'in the manner of a doctor', i.e. A LA MO, French 'a la' followed by its object.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas mission in San Antonio was besieged in 1836; Crockett died defending it.

clue.text: Could be a circular plug

parts.note: a circular is a leaflet sent round, and a plug is a promotional mention, so both describe a public notice selling something, not a round stopper

explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet mailed to many people or a plug on air is a kind of promotional notice.

clue.text: Deem notes best way to settle

indicators.note: the best way to arrange things implies a new ordering of these letters

explanation.surface: Think banknotes are the best method of paying up.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle up means to pay what is owed, the idiom for clearing accounts.

clue.text: Sets off with girlfriends to tour the school

indicators.note: one thing touring goes all round another, so it surrounds it

parts.note: dates are romantic partners, people one goes out with
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A trip starts out with the girlfriends visiting a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode a bomb is to set it off, a synonym in the verb form.

clue.text: Time to start to relax, kid

indicators.note: placed at the start, so this letter comes first

parts.note: to ease is to relax or slacken

explanation.surface: It is time to begin unwinding, child.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease or rib them playfully, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Initially announces the master of ceremonies

parts.note: the initial letters of the defining phrase, M and C, are spoken out as their letter names

explanation.surface: The host first makes the announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letters M C out loud as words and you get the spelling of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An American term for the host of a show, formed from the letters MC.

clue.text: Quarters provided by the bank

parts.note: living quarters moored by a river bank, not a financial institution handing out coins

explanation.definitionFit: A floating home moored alongside a riverbank provides lodging beside the bank.

clue.text: Land-holdings made sure, following net return

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow, coming after the turned word
a return sends the word back, so net is read backwards
made here means produced anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Property titles were secured after the net profit came back.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods or rights of holding land or property are tenancies under a feudal system.

clue.text: Others take exercise in moderation

indicators.note: one word taking another holds it inside itself

parts.note: the rest means the others
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Other people do their workouts in moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-restraint means holding back, keeping things moderate.

clue.text: Strengthen dispute in foreign currency

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, as a quarrel inside the coin

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Bolstering an argument over money from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To make stiffer is to make firmer or stronger, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Revolutionary soft, hairy shrub

indicators.note: revolutionary letters are turned round and overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A radical describes a fuzzy, downy bush.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered ornamental bush is a common garden shrub.

clue.text: Accelerates degrees at university

parts.note: steps are stages or degrees in a scale
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student speeds through the degree stages at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the pace or intensity is to speed things along.

clue.text: In prison, one captured by firearm gets bird

parts.note: pen is an enclosure, slang for a penitentiary

indicators.note: being captured by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An inmate seized at gunpoint ends up with a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets bird' plays on 'bird' as British slang for prison time, but here bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless seabird of the southern hemisphere is still a bird.

clue.text: Soldiers included in new rises — sharp rises

indicators.note: being included in something means being put inside it
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are involved in fresh increases, steep ascents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' appears twice: the first is the fodder for 'new', the second belongs to the definition, mountain ranges being sharp rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Jagged mountain ranges are steep peaks rising sharply, from Spanish for saw.

clue.text: Be prepared to defend

definitions.meaning: be ready and waiting to act
support or stick up for someone loyally

explanation.surface: The scout motto followed by a duty of protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to wait in readiness and to remain loyal to someone.

clue.text: Notes, possibly Roman made

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Written jottings perhaps produced by an ancient Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a written reminder or internal message, these are notes.

clue.text: Animal's low points

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A creature's lowest spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American deer is an animal.

clue.text: A month to live, perhaps

parts.note: May is a month
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: Someone may have a month left to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means possibly, exactly as perhaps does.

clue.text: A month in advance

definitions.meaning: the third month of the year
to go forward steadily, as troops do

explanation.surface: Getting ahead by a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the spring month and also means to walk forward in step.

clue.text: One chap returns, holding ring for girl

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it
returns means the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: a man is a chap
O is shaped like a ring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man comes back with a ring for his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN holding O gives MOAN; I plus MOAN read backwards by 'returns' gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical woman's name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Was inadequate as an air gunner — fell short as a pilot

definitions.text: Was inadequate as an air gunner
definitions.meaning: fired below the target, missing it

explanation.surface: An aircrew member failed both as gunner and as pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means aimed too low or landed short of the target.

clue.text: Narrowly failed, received a school caning

definitions.meaning: lost a race by a tiny margin
was hit on the head, taken literally, as a pupil punished

explanation.surface: A pupil just missed out and then got punished at school.
explanation.definitionFit: The racing idiom means losing by a very small margin, and literally describes a beating.
